name: progress-track-sentinel
rationale: The loop-free entry unconditionally stores uint sentinel 0xffffffff to its sole four-byte read/write progress buffer; one invocation changes every poisoned output byte.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-float-64-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry, whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (offset 0, 256 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[k][n] (row stride w_ld = 64 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in float and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the float inputs.

Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links three translation units, each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule and the matmul2d lowering. Replaced: the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: local-convolution-data-gradient-3x3-writes-every-channel
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-destination case of this entry, whose zero extents fail the entry's bounds check before any work. srcSizes = (C, W, H, N) = (3, 5, 4, 1), dilation (2, 1), a 3x3 kernel, format 1; one threadgroup of 15x4 threads, one per (w * C + c, h): each walks the 3x3 window backwards (tap index from 8 down), sums the in-bounds products, and writes coordinate (c, w, h, n), so table entry 1's words 0 to 2 (c) are written and words 3 to 5 keep the 0xab fill. The retained modules of the source callbacks the case links return constants (prefixPrimary_f 1.0, prefixSecondary_f and prefixTertiary_f 0.0; the only retained modules of those functions), so every tap's product is 0.0 and every sum is exactly +0.0 in any order: the variant observes the loops, the bounds checks, and which destination coordinates the kernel writes, not data-dependent arithmetic. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the tap loops run kernelHeight = 3 by kernelWidth = 3 times (function constants 1 and 0), the channel loop C = 3 times, and one thread runs per grid position. The linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec) stores to table entry 1 at the coordinate's first component only, and every write in this case stores the same value, so the observed words do not depend on write order.

name: linked-k48-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-half-16-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry, whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48 (one whole 32-deep block, the unsafe loader, and a 16-deep remainder, the safe one). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (expert strides w, scales and biases batch stride = N*K = 768), writing only its own rows. W[e][k][n] (w_ld = 16 bytes): both experts hold q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads); expert 0's scales repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and expert 1's are half of them (biases unread without the bias bit). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . W/2 = a . W): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (64 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Each dequantized weight is a multiple of 0.25 at most 30, exact in half, and each x at most 10; each product with x a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-half-16-non-transposed

rationale: The non-transposed half 16 counterpart of the committed mps_gather_qmm_rhs_t_bfloat_64 case: mps_gather_qmm_rhs_n_half_16 with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule and the matmul2d lowering. name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nineteen

name: two-lanes-four-passes-k14-of-21-indices
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-width case, whose K = 0 and srcWidth = 0 skip every read and write. Here MPSTopKParameters (binding 29) holds K = 14, srcWidth = 21, srcHeight = 1; kMPSUserConstant = 1 selects the index output (kFindIndices = 1) and all four passes (kKU4O4 = 0). Dispatch: 2 threads along x in one threadgroup. The retained links fix the data: the 4-wide loop (prefixPrimary_4xf, module returns zeroinitializer) covers columns 0 to 15 in 2 step(s) of 4 * tgSize, and the scalar tail (prefixPrimary_f, module returns 1.0) covers columns 16 to 20, so the row is 16 zeros then 5 ones. Each thread keeps a top 4 (strict ogt to enter, strict olt to reorder), the threadgroup merges lists in a halving tree through threadgroup memory (the own entry wins only when strictly greater, so ties take the partner's), and thread 0 writes columns 4 * pass + i for i < K - 4 * pass whose index is not -1; later passes exclude the indices earlier passes returned. Expected columns: [17, 19, 16, 18, 20, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15, 0, 'fill', 'fill']. The indices pin the AIR's own tie rule, which is deterministic: every value is 0 or 1, conversions of small indices are exact, and every exchange is barrier-separated with fixed partners, with no atomics. Two lanes (or a single pass) keep the kernel race-free: with more lanes and several passes, the next pass's merge writes could reach the broadcast index slots before a slower thread reads them. The loops are bounded by srcWidth = 21 (4-wide steps and the scalar tail), by log2 of the lane count (merge rounds), by 4 (insertion and write loops) and by the pass count; each observed column is written at most once, by thread 0.

name: two-lanes-four-passes-k16-of-11-values

The values do not depend on tie order: the count of ones and zeros fixes every written word, and the unwritten columns keep the 0xab fill. Two lanes (or a single pass) keep the kernel race-free: with more lanes and several passes, the next pass's merge writes could reach the broadcast index slots before a slower thread reads them. The loops are bounded by srcWidth = 11 (4-wide steps and the scalar tail), by log2 of the lane count (merge rounds), by 4 (insertion and write loops) and by the pass count; each observed column is written at most once, by thread 0.

name: prune-the-two-smallest-magnitudes-of-a-float4
rationale: isFloat selects the float arm, so the one invocation takes air.fast_fabs.v4f32 of [3, -1, 2, -4] and zeroes the two smallest-magnitude lanes of the original vector. The answer is a permutation of the input with two lanes replaced, so it is exact whatever fabs costs, and it pins which two lanes the unrolled two-smallest scan selects and that their signs come from the unmodified vector.

name: prune-the-two-smallest-magnitudes-of-a-half4
rationale: isFloat is false, so the same entry takes the half arm and air.fabs.v4f16 of [3, -1, 2, -4] selects the same two lanes to zero in the original half4. Paired with prune-the-two-smallest-magnitudes-of-a-float4 on the identical inputs, the two cases differ only in the function constant, so a specialization that picks the wrong arm, or reads the gated buffer at the other element width, changes the bytes.
